audience: developers, founders and teams shipping AI-assisted software

states.label: Unknown
states.meaning: The current state cannot be established with reliable information or evidence.

states.label: Claimed
states.meaning: The practice is asserted, but there is no durable implementation or test evidence.

states.label: Implemented
states.meaning: The practice is present in the product or workflow and there is observable implementation evidence.

states.label: Verified
states.meaning: A recent direct test, review or reproducible artefact supports the claim; structured input requires an evidence note.

states.label: Not applicable
states.meaning: The control genuinely does not apply to this product or workflow; only allowed where the control permits it and a rationale is required.

domains.title: AI agents, MCP and tool access

items.prompt: A named human owns the release decision and remains accountable for AI-assisted changes.
items.recommended_action: Name the human release owner and record who can approve or reject security-sensitive changes.

items.prompt: The team can explain the deployed architecture, trust boundaries, data flows and external services without relying on the AI tool to reconstruct them.
items.recommended_action: Maintain a concise architecture/data-flow record covering entry points, storage, external services and trust boundaries.

items.prompt: Plausible abuse cases and security-relevant trust assumptions have been identified before public release.
items.recommended_action: Write down the most important attacker goals, trust assumptions and failure modes; convert them into checks.

items.prompt: AI-assisted edits are reviewed as diffs, including unexpected or out-of-scope changes.
items.recommended_action: Require review of the complete diff and reject unrelated generated changes instead of accepting a large opaque patch.
evidence_examples: review record referencing the complete diff

items.prompt: Authentication uses established mechanisms and security-sensitive identity flows are not improvised by generated code.
items.recommended_action: Use maintained authentication libraries or platform mechanisms and review login, recovery and session flows.

items.prompt: Authorization is enforced server-side for every protected action and object, not only in the UI.
items.recommended_action: Add server-side permission checks at the resource/action boundary and test denied paths.

items.prompt: Cross-user, cross-tenant and object-level isolation has been tested with negative cases where relevant.
items.recommended_action: Test whether one identity can read or change another identity's objects by modifying identifiers, routes or API calls.

items.prompt: Administrative, recovery and other high-impact functions have stronger access boundaries and are not protected by obscurity.
items.recommended_action: Inventory privileged functions, require explicit authorization and verify recovery/admin flows separately.

items.prompt: Secrets are not hard-coded, committed, shipped to clients or pasted into AI prompts/context; production credentials are stored and scoped appropriately.
items.recommended_action: Move secrets to an appropriate secret store, rotate exposed credentials and add repository/context exclusions.

items.prompt: AI tools receive only the minimum project context needed and sensitive files are excluded from tool context where supported.
items.recommended_action: Configure AI-tool ignore/exclusion rules and avoid exposing keys, private data, production dumps or regulated content to unnecessary context.

items.prompt: Sensitive data is minimized, protected in transit and storage, and excluded or redacted from logs where appropriate.
items.recommended_action: Document sensitive data, remove unnecessary collection and verify encryption, access and logging behaviour.

items.prompt: Important persistent data has a recovery path that has been tested, and destructive operations have defined safeguards.
items.recommended_action: Test restoration of important data and define confirmation/rollback or equivalent safeguards for destructive actions.
evidence_examples: restore test or destructive-action recovery evidence

items.prompt: Every AI-suggested external package is verified to exist in the intended registry and is reviewed before installation.
items.recommended_action: Verify package name, registry, maintainer/history and project relevance before adding it.

items.prompt: Dependency versions are reproducibly resolved and known-vulnerability checks run before release.
items.recommended_action: Commit lockfiles or equivalent resolution data and run ecosystem-appropriate vulnerability checks in CI.

items.prompt: Dependencies are minimized and material new dependencies have a recorded purpose, licence and maintenance/provenance check.
items.recommended_action: Remove unnecessary packages and record why material dependencies are trusted and needed.

items.prompt: CI/CD actions, build plugins and automation dependencies are pinned or otherwise controlled, and their privileges are minimized.
items.recommended_action: Review pipeline dependencies and permissions; pin immutable versions where practical and restrict tokens.

items.prompt: Untrusted input is validated to expected shape and length, and output/query contexts use safe encoding or parameterization.
items.recommended_action: Define input contracts and use framework-safe rendering, parameterized queries and context-appropriate encoding.

items.prompt: High-risk parsers and sinks such as URLs, files, shell commands and server-side fetches have explicit validation and isolation.
items.recommended_action: Review file upload, SSRF, command execution and parser boundaries; remove unsafe generic execution paths.

items.prompt: Security- and money-relevant business invariants are enforced on the server and tested against replay, concurrency or identifier tampering where relevant.
items.recommended_action: Encode critical invariants in server-side logic and add negative/idempotency/concurrency tests for high-impact state transitions.

items.prompt: Externally reachable operations have appropriate resource limits, rate controls, timeouts and fail-safe behaviour.
items.recommended_action: Set bounded request/body/job limits, rate controls and timeouts for abuse-prone or expensive operations.

items.prompt: AI coding agents run with the minimum filesystem, shell, network, cloud and repository privileges needed for the task.
items.recommended_action: Separate development from production credentials and sandbox or scope agent access to the current task.

items.prompt: Destructive, credential-sensitive and security-boundary changes require deliberate human approval rather than blanket auto-accept.
items.recommended_action: Disable unrestricted auto-approval and define operations that always require human confirmation.

items.prompt: MCP servers and other connected tools are explicitly trusted, minimally permissioned and use scoped credentials.
items.recommended_action: Maintain a tool allowlist, review each tool's capabilities and restrict credentials and network reach.

items.prompt: Issues, pull requests, repository files, logs and fetched web content are treated as untrusted instructions when consumed by an AI agent.
items.recommended_action: Review untrusted context before agent use, limit context/egress and inspect resulting changes for indirect prompt injection effects.

items.prompt: Production configuration is hardened: debug/test features and default credentials are disabled or removed.
items.recommended_action: Create a repeatable production-hardening checklist and verify effective runtime configuration.

items.prompt: External exposure is intentional: TLS, cookies, CORS, security headers, origins and public endpoints are configured to the product's needs.
items.recommended_action: Inventory internet-facing endpoints and verify transport/browser/security-boundary settings instead of accepting generated defaults.

items.prompt: Databases, object storage, queues and administrative services are not publicly exposed unless explicitly required and protected.
items.recommended_action: Verify network exposure, cloud IAM and service credentials from the deployed environment.

items.prompt: Operational logging, alerting, rollback and incident ownership exist for material failures after release.
items.recommended_action: Define what will be monitored, who receives alerts, how a bad release is rolled back and who owns incident decisions.

items.prompt: Security-critical paths have automated positive and negative tests, including denial cases rather than only happy paths.
items.recommended_action: Add tests that prove unauthorized, malformed and unsafe actions fail as intended.
evidence_examples: CI test run with named negative security tests

items.prompt: Security-sensitive AI-generated changes receive review that is independent of the same generation step.
items.recommended_action: Use a human reviewer and/or deterministic security tooling; do not treat the generating model's self-review as sole assurance.

items.prompt: Secret, dependency and code/configuration security checks run before release, and suppressions have an owner and rationale.
items.recommended_action: Run appropriate automated checks in CI and record why any security finding is suppressed or accepted.
evidence_examples: CI security-check results and exception record

items.prompt: The release can be tied to a commit, build/configuration state, dependency set, known gaps and a reproducible gate result.
items.recommended_action: Produce a small release evidence bundle so a later reviewer can reconstruct what was shipped and why it passed the gate.
